translation:
Pachiyapura

At present only about one devotee from Surat lives there; earlier, devotees used to live there. This is mentioned in an article by a doctor of that place, published in an issue of Janakalyan (a magazine), somewhere in its Year 4 to Year 6, which wrote that in this village there was the house of a Kabir-panthi (follower of the Kabir path) devotee. At their home there was a mud grain-bin (kothi); it never needed to be refilled with fresh grain — rather, grain was taken out daily from its lower compartment to run a sadavrat (a continuous free food distribution). That house and grain-bin were destroyed when a flood came in a certain year. So at present there is nothing there except perhaps a single devotee. Thus this can be said to be our punya sthali (a place of religious merit). In Udadharma, Edition 1, and in Bhajan Sagar, three devotees from this village are counted.
